title: Infrared infrastructure snapshot (extractor output)
description: One JSON document describing a project's infrastructure as FACTS. The extractor (colleague A) writes it; the decision engine (colleague B) reads it. It deliberately contains no findings, scores, recommendations or 'issues': the engine derives all of those itself (otherwise the engine would be graded on the extractor's opinions, and two engines could never be compared on the same input). Fields outside `usage`, `cost` and `edges[].gb_month` are configuration facts read from the provider API and are 'observed' by definition. Unknown values are omitted or null, never guessed. Extension fields must start with 'x_'. Schema version 1.1 adds optional AI consumption, database statistics, and CI runner fields.

schema_version.description: Semver major.minor. Additive changes bump minor; anything that removes/renames/retypes a field bumps major. Engine must accept any 1.x. Version 1.1 adds AI consumption, database statistics, and CI runners.

extractor.description: Name of the extractor, e.g. 'infrared-extractor' or 'hand-written-mock'.

endpoint.description: API endpoint scanned, e.g. http://localhost:4566 for Floci; null for mocks.

is_mock.description: True when the document was written by hand, not extracted.

stacks.description: Optional logical groupings (team/product/environment). Components reference one by id via `stack`.

controls.description: Account-level security/ops controls that are NOT tied to one component. Used by security gates in the forecast. null = could not be determined.

backup_plans_exist.description: Any AWS Backup plan or equivalent.

edges.description: Directed dependencies. `from` depends on / calls / writes to `to`. Parent/child containment (cluster -> node group) is NOT an edge: use `parent`.

ai_consumption.description: Optional AI/ML consumption metrics: token spend per model and provider, GPU utilization. Added in schema 1.1.

tokens_by_model.description: Token consumption per model and provider

ci_runners.description: Optional GitHub runner statistics. Added in schema 1.1.

stay_together.description: Optional hints: sets of components that should be moved as one unit or kept within one failure domain (chatty, transactional or latency-bound). The engine may also derive groups from edges; hints from the extractor/owner win.

scope.description: Boundary the members must NOT be split across: 'zone' = same AZ, 'region' = same region, 'provider' = same provider (moving one means moving all).

id.description: Lowercase slug, unique within the document.

provenance.description: observed = read as-is from the system's API/metrics. estimated = computed by the extractor from observed inputs with a stated formula (e.g. list price x hours). synthetic = injected fake data (Floci has no real telemetry/billing; its metrics come from synth/metrics.py). The engine must carry the weakest provenance of the inputs it used into the confidence of every recommendation.

static_metric.description: A single point value with provenance (capacity, size, cost, edge volume).

basis.description: For estimated values: how it was computed, e.g. 'list price 4.032 USD/h x 730 h x 0.92 EUR/USD'.

series_metric.description: Summary of a time series over a window. Values are PER UNIT when the component has quantity > 1 (e.g. cpu_pct is the per-instance average). `sum` is over the whole window; the engine scales to a month with 30/window_days.

unit.description: e.g. percent, count, bytes, gb, iops, per_second, messages, ms

resolution_seconds.description: Datapoint period used to compute avg/p95/max, e.g. 3600.

basis.description: Source, e.g. 'CloudWatch AWS/RDS CPUUtilization, Average, period 3600'.

name.description: Human name / the provider's own identifier.

kind.description: Provider-neutral class. The catalog maps each kind to per-provider options, so this list must match catalog `kind` exactly. `container` = a containerised service (ECS/Fargate service, Cloud Run); `node_group` = a pool of worker nodes whose `parent` is a kubernetes_cluster; `other` for anything not worth modelling (put what it is in `service`).

service.description: Provider service, e.g. rds, aurora-postgresql, eks-managed-nodegroup, ecs-fargate, dynamodb, s3.

sku.description: Provider size/class, e.g. db.r5.8xlarge, m5.8xlarge, '4vcpu/16GB'. Free text; the engine uses `capacity` for sizing, not this.

quantity.description: Number of identical units this component stands for (12 nodes, 3 NAT gateways, 8 tasks). `usage` is per unit; `cost.monthly_eur` and `capacity` x quantity are totals/per-unit as documented on each field.

region.description: Provider region id (eu-west-1) or a site id for on-prem (onprem-dc1). Floci only has us-east-1; mocks may set others by hand to exercise residency constraints.

zones.description: Number of availability zones the component actually runs in (placement, not what the service could do). 1 = single-AZ.

status.description: active = in use. idle = running and attached but doing ~nothing over the window. orphan = not referenced by anything / not attached (unattached volume, copy nobody connects to). The extractor sets this from API facts (attachment state, zero connections over the window); the engine decides what to do about it.

stateful.description: Holds data that must be migrated, not just redeployed.

data_gb.description: Data actually stored (not allocated). unit: GB.

data_classification.description: From tags where present; otherwise 'unknown'. Never guess pii from a name.

capacity.description: PER-UNIT provisioned/allocated capacity as static metrics. Conventional keys (extend freely): vcpu, memory_gb, storage_gb, disk_gb, gpus, provisioned_iops, provisioned_rcu, provisioned_wcu, shards, throughput_mibps, object_count, timeout_s.

usage.description: PER-UNIT observed load as series summaries. Conventional keys: cpu_pct, memory_pct, gpu_pct, connections, read_iops, write_iops, network_in_gb, network_out_gb, requests, invocations, duration_ms, messages_sent, messages_received, messages_visible, consumed_rcu, consumed_wcu, throttled_requests, incoming_bytes_per_s, hit_rate_pct, evictions.

engine.description: Database/engine or runtime and version (postgres 11.22, kubernetes 1.28, python3.8).

features_used.description: Extensions/capabilities the workload actually relies on (pgvector, pg_partman, logical_replication, postgis). Engine rules out targets whose catalog `features_supported` lacks any of them.

security.description: Facts needed for hard security gates. null = unknown.

world_open_ports.description: Ports reachable from 0.0.0.0/0 via attached security groups. -1 means every port.

plaintext_secrets_suspected.description: Heuristic: secret-looking values in env vars / parameters.

admin_privileges.description: Attached role grants Action:* on Resource:*.

cost.description: OPTIONAL. Floci has no billing, so extractors normally estimate from list prices. The engine must not depend on it: it prices the catalog itself and uses this only to cross-check the current-state baseline.

monthly_eur.description: TOTAL for all `quantity` units, in EUR/month.

db_stats.description: Optional database statistics for postgres components. Schemas and statistics only, never table rows. Added in schema 1.1.

indexes.description: Total index count across all tables

config.description: Raw service settings as read from the API (visibility_timeout_s, partition_key, k8s_version, ...). Opaque to the schema; engine rules may read documented keys (see README) but must tolerate absence.

kind.description: traffic = user/request path (LB -> backend). data = reads/writes a datastore. event = async messaging (queue, notification, schedule). network = placement/reachability only (SG, subnet, VPC attachment). dns = name resolution. config = references via env/parameter.

evidence.description: declared = explicit in config (target group, event mapping, env var). observed = seen in flow logs/metrics. inferred = extractor guess.

gb_month.description: OPTIONAL monthly volume. Floci produces no traffic data, so this is estimated or synthetic there; omit rather than invent when unknown. Used for egress cost; kind and stay_together decide which components move together.
